title: Trouble setting up multiple respawning resource nodes

posts.author: Shy_Yhormie
posts.body: Hello, I'm a first time poster and semi-new to RPG Maker in general. I'm currently trying to set up multiple respawning resource nodes. Since I plan on having quite a few I've tried making a couple of common events with self-switches so each node will have it's own respawn time. I have a harvest common event that works properly, but the respawn counter common event seems to not turn off, even after the correct number of respawn hours pass. I've tried quite a few different ways of writing these events as well, and they either get stuck on the "Node is empty" message, or end up "dead" after the first node usage. I've tried a couple of tutorials, scouring the forum, and spending a few hours experimenting but I can't figure it out on my own currently. Thanks in advance for any help! I can attach pictures tomorrow, as I haven't been able to figure out how to screenshot a single screen since I got a second one for the life of me and I am posting this before bed and don't feel like booting up my laptop lol.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Did you make a control switch called "Self Switch A"? Control switches are supposed to be global, self switches are to track changes on individual events. Every event has self switches, so making a global switch called that doesn't tell you which event's self switch it is.
There is also no reason to be using up several global variables to track the respawn time of one event. You only need to count frames, which represent 1/60th of a second. If the respawn time is one minute then you would count down 360 frames.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Set the second event page to parallel, put Wait:360 frames, then Self Switch A: OFF
That will set it back to the first event page after a minute. Change 360 to whatever number of frames you want the respawn time to be.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: It's not simple because now you're introducing variable times and events that can remotely affect the timers on other events. You'd have to keep a list of every event with a timer then loop through it to add/subtract from those timers. It's basically what Trihan's script does and he already wrote it so no reason to write it again.
